title: Two layers of insulation
prompt: A steady one-dimensional heat flow crosses two layers in perfect contact. They have equal area 0.50 m², thicknesses 2.0 and 3.0 cm, and thermal conductivities 0.20 and 0.60 W/(m K), respectively. The outside faces are held at 40 and 10 °C, with the first layer on the hot side. Find the heat flow and interface temperature. Check what changes when the layer order is reversed.

answer:
Use series thermal resistances:

\[
R_i=\frac{L_i}{k_i A}, \qquad \dot Q=\frac{\Delta T}{R_1+R_2}
\]

Given:

- \(A=0.50\ \text{m}^2\)
- \(L_1=2.0\ \text{cm}=0.020\ \text{m},\quad k_1=0.20\ \text{W/(m K)}\)
- \(L_2=3.0\ \text{cm}=0.030\ \text{m},\quad k_2=0.60\ \text{W/(m K)}\)
- Hot face \(T_h=40^\circ\text{C}\), cold face \(T_c=10^\circ\text{C}\)

Resistances:

\[
R_1=\frac{0.020}{0.20(0.50)}=0.20\ \text{K/W}
\]

\[
R_2=\frac{0.030}{0.60(0.50)}=0.10\ \text{K/W}
\]

Total resistance:

\[
R_\text{tot}=0.20+0.10=0.30\ \text{K/W}
\]

Heat flow:

\[
\dot Q=\frac{40-10}{0.30}=100\ \text{W}
\]

Heat flux:

\[
q''=\frac{\dot Q}{A}=\frac{100}{0.50}=200\ \text{W/m}^2
\]

Interface temperature, with layer 1 on the hot side:

\[
T_i=T_h-\dot Q R_1
=40-(100)(0.20)=20^\circ\text{C}
\]

or equivalently,

\[
T_i=T_c+\dot Q R_2
=10+(100)(0.10)=20^\circ\text{C}
\]

So:

\[
\boxed{\dot Q=100\ \text{W},\qquad T_i=20^\circ\text{C}}
\]

Direction: from the \(40^\circ\text{C}\) face toward the \(10^\circ\text{C}\) face.

### If the layer order is reversed

The total thermal resistance remains the same:

\[
R_\text{tot}=0.10+0.20=0.30\ \text{K/W}
\]

so the heat flow is unchanged:

\[
\boxed{\dot Q=100\ \text{W}}
\]

But now the \(3.0\ \text{cm}\), \(k=0.60\ \text{W/(m K)}\) layer is on the hot side. Its resistance is \(0.10\ \text{K/W}\), so:

\[
T_i=40-(100)(0.10)=30^\circ\text{C}
\]

Thus, when reversed:

\[
\boxed{\dot Q=100\ \text{W},\qquad T_i=30^\circ\text{C}}
\]

Final answers:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Original order: } \dot Q=100\ \text{W},\quad T_i=20^\circ\text{C}\\
&\text{Reversed order: } \dot Q=100\ \text{W},\quad T_i=30^\circ\text{C}
\end{aligned}}
\]

The heat flow is unchanged because the same two thermal resistances are in series; only the interface temperature changes.
